smbd_deltas: the smbd challenge rip and the nes rip are the same level. the smbd one is 140 columns and starts at what is column 16 here - all eleven of its solid blocks (seven firebar pivots and four lone ones), both roof stubs, every lava pit, the bridge, the axe and bowser sit exactly sixteen columns left of their nes cells, and a cell-by-cell diff of the 140 x 13 overlap comes out clean apart from tiles a flame or a sprite is drawn over. so nothing in 1-4 moved between smb1 and smbd, and columns 0-15 - the opening raised platform, its three descending steps and the first lava pit - are transcribed off the nes rip, which is the only one that draws them. the two rips do differ past the axe: the nes one draws the toad room's ceiling and its two sprites out to column 157, the smbd one stops the roof at 143 and shapes the room differently. none of that is walkable - the engine's castle ends on the axe - so the bible stops at 152. challenge mode's own additions, five red coins and the yoshi egg replacing the ladder's top-middle coin, are recorded in "smbd" and are not compiled.
confidence_notes:
1-4 is transcribed cell by cell from the two map rips above, the way 1-1, 1-2 and 1-3 were: every 16x16 cell of both images was hashed and classified against a tile sheet cut from the same image (75 distinct tiles across the nes rip's 158 level columns, 63 across the smbd rip's 140), the two classifications were diffed column by column, and they agree everywhere they overlap (see smbd_deltas). the nes rip is grid-aligned with no offset - image row 13 is the ground row this schema names - and its columns 156-207 are the ripper's caption and legend, not level. the smbd rip is offset sixteen columns right and one row down and carries no grid row 0, which holds nothing but sky.

the firebar count is measured and settles what the prose pass guessed at: the rips draw eleven of the castle's lone solid blocks and exactly seven of them carry a flame chain, which is the seven mariowiki names. the two rips caught the bars at different angles (the nes one diagonal, the smbd one straight down) yet the same seven have bars and the same four do not, so the four are blocks and not bars whose chain happened to be hidden inside masonry. each drawn chain reaches three cells from its pivot, which is six segments at the 8 px spacing hazards.c uses, so every "length": 6 is measured.

what is not measured: each bar's rotation speed and direction. a still frame cannot show either. all seven are written "slow" (physics.json's 0x28) because smb1's fast bar is a later-castle object, and six are written "cw" against one "ccw" at 88/4 - the nes rip has six bars at the same down-right angle and that one at its exact mirror, which is what two bars turning opposite ways from a shared phase look like, but which of the two senses is the clockwise one is a coin flip. speed and direction are therefore the level's one "approx" pair even though the entries carry a measured pivot.

the prose pass got three things wrong that the rips settle. there is no horizontal lift over the bridge: the cell it was read out of (138-139 at row 6) is a bowser fireball in flight in the nes rip and is classified as one outright in the smbd rip, and the level has no lift anywhere - which is why its bridge gap carries "lift": false, to keep the compiler's wide-castle-gap deck out of a measured pit. the six coins before bowser are hidden blocks in two ranks of three, not a row of six. and the level has four lava pits, not the one the prose named.

the engine's own compromises, all of them documented rather than hidden: the ground rows 13-14 are castle masonry in the rip and are stamped as such here, so the level has no BLOCK_GROUND cell at all; the four pits are still written as gap runs, because gap is the primitive that fills a castle pit with lava. hazards.c runs one shared spin phase per rate rather than one accumulator per bar, so two bars of the same rate and handedness always point the same way; m21 made every bar whose sweep can reach the view live, drawn and able to burn, so the pair at 84 and 88 - four columns apart - both turn and both burn, and the draw is capped at two full bars nearest the camera centre. and bowser's patrol runs from his measured cell out to the bridge's last column, which keeps him over the deck; the rip catches him at one instant and cannot show how far he paces.
